> **WARNING**: Unfortunately **at this point in time** both the @Nomadcxx and @Yukaii solutions are fundamentally broken - their requests do not utilize caching properly and spam conversations, resulting in a simple prompt generating $150 usage on a cursor (ultra / team) subscription in <5 minutes.

Maybe @Yukaii solution has this but loop guard and a few more defensive functions avoid this in [open-cursor](https://github.com/Nomadcxx/opencode-cursor) BUT fundamentally **I agree with your overall sentiment** and here is why:

**Cursor-agent is essentially a black box** it doesn't speak opencodes tool protocol. So each round, the plugin has to take the full conversation history — tool definitions, results, prior calls — and flatten it all into a serialised text prompt that cursor-agent can understand (it often fails). Tool names get aliased too (cursor-agent uses its own naming like runcommand instead of bash, listdirectory instead of ls, etc, there's about 50 of these mappings and some for proprietary tools like semsearch).

When cursor-agent streams its response back, tge plugin **intercepts the SSE stream in real-time, picks out tool calls as they arrive, translate the names back, and decide per-call whether opencode should execute it or let cursor-agent handle** it (e.g. for MCP tools like Playwright). The guard sits in this interception layer, fingerprinting each call (tool + args + result type) across rounds. cursor-agent does get the full history back each round, **but it sometimes gets stuck in loops anyway repeating the same failing call despite seeing the prior failures in its context.** The guard is the only circuit breaker against this **BUT** even here it's not fully reliable because of cursor-agent 

This is exactly why I want to abandon this streaming approach for an ACP/MCP solution in next phase https://github.com/Nomadcxx/opencode-cursor?tab=readme-ov-file#roadmap . I've thought about this a lot and if next iteration can't fix it then my recommendation to maintainers is to avoid cursor support at this stage.

Thanks for the review @rekram1-node makes total sense to not elevate Kilo as a recommended provider. I'll strip all the auth.ts and dialog-provider.tsx changes.

On fetchKiloModels() and the database injection — the reason I added those is that models.dev currently points Kilo to npm: "opencode-kilo-auth" (the JungHoonGhae plugin). That package isn't in BUNDLED_PROVIDERS and doesn't export a standard create* function, so getSDK() falls through to BunProc.install → dynamic import → fn3 is not a function. That's the exact error @smetanokr is reporting above and I get the same error with models.dev approach just merged from @Daltonganger.

The CUSTOM_LOADERS entry (which you flagged as fine) adds baseURL and headers, but it doesn't override api.npm on individual models — so the broken npm path persists.

 I think the cleanest fix is:
1. Fix models.dev to use npm: "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible" (or remove the npm field entirely so it hits the fallback) — I can open a PR there
2. Strip this PR down to just the CUSTOM_LOADERS entry

That way models.dev provides the model catalog, CUSTOM_LOADERS provides the SDK wiring, and it all works without fetchKiloModels(). If you're adding dynamic model fetching for all primary providers this week, Kilo would get that for free too.

Hi! I’m seeing what looks like a **Web UI-only session list scoping/refresh bug** after upgrading **OpenCode 1.2.5 -> 1.2.6**.

## Environment
- OpenCode: **1.2.6**
- OS: Linux
- Storage: SQLite at `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`
- Important: **Sessions show correctly in the TUI**, but **not in the Web UI**.

## My setup / workflow
- I start OpenCode Web from a “neutral” directory (not inside a repo), e.g. `~/safe`:
  - `opencode web`
- In the Web UI, I then select/navigate to various projects.
- One of those projects is a git repo that uses **multiple git worktrees**:
  - main repo: `~/dev/sfp-3pl-approval`
  - worktrees live under: `~/dev/_wt/sfp-3pl-approval-*`
- Each worktree directory has its own sessions historically, and Web UI used to show them.

## Problem
After upgrading to **1.2.6**, when I’m in the Web UI and select the `~/dev/sfp-3pl-approval` project:
- the **Web UI session list shows only 1 (or almost none) of the existing sessions**
- BUT the **TUI/CLI still lists all the sessions correctly**, including those in the worktree directories

So sessions don’t seem lost—Web UI just isn’t showing them.

## Repro steps
1. Start web server from a directory outside the project:
   - `opencode web` (started from `~/safe`)
2. In the web UI, select project `~/dev/sfp-3pl-approval`
3. Observe the session list (nearly empty / missing lots of sessions)
4. Compare with TUI/CLI:
   - `(cd ~/dev/sfp-3pl-approval && opencode session list -n 50)`
   - sessions appear as expected there

## Evidence: sessions exist in DB for the worktree directories
These show that many sessions exist for the repo + worktrees:

    opencode db "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, directory FROM session WHERE directory LIKE '%sfp-3pl-approval%' GROUP BY directory ORDER BY n DESC;"

Example output (abridged):
- `~/dev/sfp-3pl-approval` -> lots of sessions
- `~/dev/_wt/sfp-3pl-approval-...` -> lots of sessions

Also, `opencode debug scrap` shows the repo worktree plus sandboxes (worktrees) are known:

    opencode debug scrap

## Additional clue: duplicate `project` rows for the same worktree path
In my DB there are **two `project` rows with the same `worktree` path** (`~/dev/sfp-3pl-approval`) but sessions are mostly associated to one of the two `project_id`s.

    opencode db "SELECT id, worktree, time_updated FROM project WHERE worktree LIKE '%/sfp-3pl-approval' ORDER BY time_updated DESC;"
    opencode db "SELECT project_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM session WHERE directory LIKE '%/dev/_wt/sfp-3pl-approval-%' GROUP BY project_id ORDER BY n DESC;"

It looks like Web UI might be picking the “wrong” project id (the one with very few sessions), so the list looks empty.

## Expected
When selecting a project in Web UI, session list should include all sessions for that project/worktree + its worktree sandboxes (as it did previously), consistent with the TUI.

## Actual
Web UI shows almost none, while TUI shows all.

If you want, I can provide more DB queries / a minimal DB snapshot (sanitized) or run with debug logging.

```
**Root Cause: Playwright MCP listTools() is hanging for ~28-30 seconds per step**

The logs tell the full story:

quirkyquarters (broken) — resolveTools takes 28-30 seconds:

19:30:48 resolveTools started
19:30:48 tool.registry task completed duration=1   ← built-in tools: instant
19:31:17 resolveTools completed duration=28425      ← 28s gap = MCP.tools()
```

And the actual SQLite issue:

```
**There's also a secondary ~7-second delay**

Before resolveTools even starts, MessageV2.filterCompacted(MessageV2.stream(sessionID)) at prompt.ts:298 loads all messages from the 4.6GB SQLite database, adding ~7 seconds per step.

Total per step: ~35 seconds of blocking
```

> The real bug is that MCP.tools() calls client.listTools() on every single step of the prompt loop, even though the tool list almost never changes mid-session.
